note: Q3 numbers are new on a thin, flat-into-print name with no guide; the only lean is the record Nordic HY issuance proxy (DCM drove Q2's Corporate Financing line) with the shares back below the incoming CEO's 7.35 purchase, offset by likely efficiency/JV one-offs and an unsourced bar, so a small positive on a 4% scale.

FY26 is pre-released and the move is in the first FY27 guide: a 21% smaller order book, worse September mortgage data and margin/incentive pressure argue for a soft volume and margin guide (the line that cost 17.5% at the interims), partly offset by a likely top-up to the GBP50m 'initial tranche' of returns on GBP158m net cash and a constructive read on the Your First Home scheme; bar unsourced, so a modest negative lean on a 6% first-guide scale.

Camissa's RNS-dated sell-down (14.5% to 10.9%, the last notice an hour before the seal, ~0.3m shares a day against 0.4m of turnover with 25m still held) is a fresh company-level overhang no broker names, landing on a stock up 15% in 20 days and positioned for further upgrades four weeks after a guide raise whose arithmetic implies H2 OP roughly flat, the exact wording that cost 9% at last year's interims; disclosed shorts rebuilding since the upgrade and a likely new buyback do not offset it.

Sourced bar (Vuma GBP238.0m at the guide midpoint) against the company's own 'Q4 started positively, strong volume momentum' and a management that has beaten at successive updates points FY26 AOP to the upper half of GBP234-242m, backed by Greggs' improving Q3 food-to-go read; it lands inside the guide and the stock is already +6% in five sessions, so a small positive, with the cash/net-debt line the two-sided risk.

A first FY27 guide plus a strategy update by an outgoing CEO on a name that has sold its last three results days 10-12% each after rallying into them, now +67% since March with an unexplained +13% on 3 Sep that smells of Shopper-disposal hope the hunter could not source a bidder for; the VDP arithmetic makes a higher FY27 guide the expected outcome rather than a surprise, and a leverage-capped buyback size only partly offsets, so a negative lean on this name's own 9-11% scale.
